strengths: Addresses a genuine practical bottleneck in diffusion LM inference with substantial throughput improvements (4.4-5.3×) demonstrated on real hardware (H100)
Well-controlled empirical evaluation across three model scales (240M-1.3B) with identical training setup, data, and tokenization
First systematic study applying SSMs/Mamba to discrete diffusion language modeling, validating that iterative denoising does not inherently require attention
Comprehensive evaluation across multiple benchmarks (validation PPL on DCLM, zero-shot generalization on 7 datasets, downstream reasoning tasks)
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and thorough related work connecting vision diffusion, SSMs, and language modeling
Hybrid architecture shows consistent improvements over pure attention, suggesting complementary roles of attention and recurrence in diffusion
weaknesses: Limited novelty: primarily an architectural replacement (Transformers → Mamba) without algorithmic innovation; bidirectional fusion (Eq. 6) is trivial (forward+backward addition)

Critical missing ablations: no analysis of (a) why additive fusion is optimal for bidirectional Mamba, (b) sensitivity to K in hybrid model (fixed at K=5), (c) impact of d_state parameter, (d) alternative fusion strategies
Modeling quality gains are inconsistent and modest: DiffuTran remains competitive at 240M; at 1.3B, ~2% PPL improvement but comparable/worse performance on individual downstream tasks
Throughput measurements limited to batch size 1 on single GPU—fails to assess practical speedup in realistic multi-batch/distributed inference scenarios; unclear if benefits persist with batching

Only compared against Transformer baseline (DiffuTran); no comparison with recently proposed efficient alternatives (approximate KV-caching methods Wu et al. 2025, Ma et al. 2025, other efficient inference techniques)

Weak absolute downstream task performance at 1.3B scale (26-38% accuracy on challenging benchmarks) makes it difficult to assess whether quality-efficiency trade-off is acceptable; paper acknowledges scores are modest but doesn't investigate implications
No theoretical analysis of why SSMs should be effective denoisers beyond citing vision diffusion; limited intuition for the mechanisms enabling performance
Missing implementation details: exact Mamba-2 training kernel, reproducibility concerns (no code release mentioned), incomplete hyperparameter documentation

strengths: Clear articulation of the quadratic attention bottleneck in diffusion LM inference and well-motivated problem statement
Controlled experimental design with identical training data, tokenization, and noise schedules across three parameter scales
Significant throughput improvements for long sequences (5.3× at 1.3B scale) with correct complexity analysis
Comprehensive evaluation including validation PPL, zero-shot generalization across 7 datasets, and downstream reasoning benchmarks
Practical exploration of hybrid Mamba-Attention architectures showing complementary benefits
weaknesses: Limited novelty: straightforward architectural replacement of Transformers with Mamba, with precedent in vision diffusion (Hu et al. 2024); essentially an engineering contribution rather than a conceptual advance
Unfair parameter comparison: DiffuApriel models are 20-23% larger than DiffuTran baselines despite claims of 'comparable' budgets, undermining core performance claims

Mixed and inconsistent quality results: pure DiffuApriel degrades perplexity at 240M scale; improvements at 1.3B require adding attention layers back (DiffuApriel-H), contradicting the core Mamba-only proposition

Critical limitation inadequately explored: paper admits advantages 'diminish on short contexts' but uses L=1024 training (relatively short) with throughput measured only up to L=65K, creating unrealistic evaluation regime
Modest downstream task improvements (~3-4% average) with absolute scores acknowledged as 'modest' (25-38% accuracy), raising questions about practical significance beyond efficiency gains
Missing comparisons with alternative efficiency approaches: no comparison with KV-caching optimizations (Ma et al., Wu et al., Nguyen-Tri et al.), sparse/linear attention, or other SSMs

Weak analysis and limited insights: no ablations on bidirectionality or K value; no linguistic analysis of what patterns Mamba captures differently; no training efficiency comparison; arbitrary design choices unexplained
Unrealistic deployment scenario: measurements use batch size 1 and single GPU; no analysis for realistic serving workloads with batch > 1
Underdeveloped discussion of limitations: short-context disadvantage treated as passing remark rather than core limitation despite being fundamental to practical deployment
Presentation issues: title 'Breaking the Bottleneck' overclaims resolution; parameter count inequalities buried in tables rather than prominently discussed early on

strengths: Addresses a real practical bottleneck in diffusion LM inference with substantial throughput improvements (up to 4.4× for pure Mamba, 2.6× for hybrid) across multiple scales

Solid controlled experimental methodology with identical training setup across variants, three model scales (240M-1.3B), and comprehensive evaluation (validation PPL, 7 zero-shot benchmarks, 6 downstream tasks)
Clear theoretical justification for efficiency gains with proper complexity analysis showing O(BLd) vs O(BL²d) scaling and well-explained hybrid complexity tradeoffs
First exploration of SSM/Mamba backbones for discrete masked diffusion in language models, successfully demonstrating drop-in replacement without altering probabilistic semantics
Consistent downstream task improvements (~3-4% over DiffuTran across benchmarks, Table 5) and competitive/better perplexity at largest scale (1.3B), particularly for hybrid variant
Clear presentation with reproducible experiments using standard benchmarks, careful wall-clock timing (CUDA graphs, 20-run averages), and detailed implementation specifications
weaknesses: Inconsistent perplexity results undermine quality claims: DiffuApriel underperforms at 240M scale (44.60 vs 43.82 under Chinchilla) and shows substantial zero-shot regressions (e.g., PTB 203.92 vs 153.47), with unclear characterization of quality-efficiency tradeoffs

Limited scale (1.3B maximum) with no comparison to larger recent DLMs (Dream-7B, LLaDA) or other DLM efficiency approaches (block diffusion, KV-caching variants), making it unclear if Mamba-based diffusion is optimal relative to alternatives

Acknowledged limitation that 'performance advantages diminish on short contexts' but paper doesn't adequately quantify this—all experiments at L=1024 context, yet gains primarily emerge at L≥2048, limiting practical applicability for many use cases

Hybrid architecture (DiffuApriel-H) lacks proper justification: K=5 fixed across all experiments without ablation or exploration of alternatives; bidirectional fusion is additive without exploring learned fusion strategies; design choices borrowed from autoregressive work unvalidated for diffusion

Parameter count mismatches complicate interpretation: DiffuTran-0.24B (0.24B) vs DiffuApriel-0.29B (0.29B) is 21% difference; 0.5B vs 0.6B is 29% difference—making unclear whether improvements stem from architecture or additional capacity

Missing critical ablations: no analysis of bidirectional design necessity, additive fusion choice, or why Mamba is suited for diffusion denoisers; no qualitative analysis of samples or human evaluation
No statistical significance testing: single run per configuration with no error bars or confidence intervals; downstream improvements of 1-2 points lack significance assessment

Inference evaluation incomplete: only batch size 1 tested (higher batches could change throughput ratios), no memory consumption analysis, sensitivity to denoising step count unexplored, no analysis of generation quality-latency tradeoffs

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three model scales with controlled setup (identical training data, tokenization, noise schedules), providing confident comparison of architectures
Excellent throughput analysis combining asymptotic complexity (Table 3) with extensive empirical measurements up to 65K tokens, demonstrating 8.2× improvements on long sequences
Insightful latency decomposition (Figure 3) that clearly isolates quadratic attention costs and explains Mamba's superior scaling behavior
Thorough breadth of evaluation: seven zero-shot datasets, five downstream reasoning tasks, and multiple inference algorithms (full-sequence and block-diffusion variants)
Well-motivated bidirectional Mamba architecture that preserves probabilistic semantics of masked diffusion while enabling linear-time inference
Clear presentation with good organization, informative visualizations, and honest discussion of limitations
weaknesses: Limited novelty: primarily combines two existing methods (Mamba + masked diffusion) without substantial architectural innovation; vision diffusion Mamba models already exist; bidirectional design is straightforward addition (Eq. 6)

Unjustified critical design choices lacking ablations: N=5 interleaving pattern (no sensitivity analysis), bidirectional fusion via simple addition (why not concatenation + projection?), halved MLP expansion ratio (impact uncharacterized)

Severe practical limitations: batch size B=1 throughout (not realistic for production), K=L/p denoising steps confounds sequence length with refinement iterations (non-standard choice), no fine-tuning evaluation

Modest scale (max 1.3B) and weak downstream absolute performance (20-38% accuracy), limiting confidence in ~4% relative improvements; unclear what drives the non-monotonic scaling of DiffuMamba (struggles at 0.5B, recovers at 1.3B) in Table 1
Inconsistent results between tables (e.g., DiffuTran's 153.47 PTB PPL vs. 43.82 validation PPL in Tables 1-2) with insufficient explanation
Limited statistical rigor: only 5 throughput runs with 3 warm-ups, no confidence intervals or significance testing; claims like '8.2×' are point estimates without uncertainty

Missing essential ablations and comparisons: no comparison with sparse or linear attention variants, no sensitivity to N value, no evaluation of bidirectional fusion alternatives, incomplete analysis of failure modes

strengths: Technically sound approach combining bidirectional Mamba with masked diffusion, well-motivated for bidirectional context requirements
Comprehensive latency decomposition analysis (Figure 3) providing mechanistic insights into performance differences
Controlled experimental setup with careful parameter matching across three architectures under identical training conditions
Systematic asymptotic complexity analysis (Table 3) combined with extensive empirical throughput benchmarking across sequence lengths up to 65K
Honest discussion of limitations in appendix (batch size B=1, lack of block-diffusion training, artificial K=L/p scaling)
DiffuMamba-H demonstrates consistent improvements at larger scales (1.3B), suggesting complementarity between Mamba and attention
weaknesses: Limited novelty: straightforward application of existing Mamba architecture to existing masked diffusion framework without significant innovation
Misleading headline claims: 8.2× speedup applies only to the least practical regime (full-sequence, K=L/8); more realistic block-AR inference shows only 2.3× speedup

Incomplete evaluation of the most important regime: paper claims block-AR is 'the only strategy that scales linearly' yet provides no evidence that models were trained for this setting, contradicting their own motivation
Scale-dependent performance failures: pure DiffuMamba underperforms DiffuTran on 4/7 datasets at 240M scale with no explanation provided for this scale-dependent behavior
Parameter count inconsistency: comparing DiffuMamba-1.6B against DiffuTran-1.3B with different MLP expansion ratios undermines fair comparison
Severely limited practical evaluation: batch size B=1 only, artificial K=L/p scaling, no evaluation of variable inference step scenarios
Missing critical comparisons: no comparison with recent DLM acceleration techniques (dKV-cache, dLLM-cache, adaptive caching) that may achieve similar speedups
Lack of ablation studies: N=5 choice for hybrid model unjustified, no sensitivity analysis, no investigation of why Mamba fails at smaller scales
Modest downstream performance: Table 4 shows only ~4% improvements on weak base model benchmarks with absolute performance in 26-38% range
No evaluation of key DLM advantages: missing tasks where parallel decoding and in-filling capabilities would be most beneficial

strengths: Clear practical contribution: 8.2× throughput improvement on long sequences addresses a real inference bottleneck for diffusion language models
Rigorous experimental methodology: Identical training conditions (data, tokenization, noise schedules) across all variants with controlled comparison focusing solely on mixer architecture

Excellent theoretical grounding: Asymptotic complexity analysis (Table 3) and latent decomposition analysis (Figure 3) provide principled understanding of efficiency gains beyond empirical measurements

Comprehensive throughput evaluation: Extended to 65K token sequences with evaluation across multiple inference algorithms (full-sequence denoising and block-AR), providing insights into when improvements manifest
Systematic evaluation across scales: Three model sizes (240M, 0.5B, 1.3B) reveal scale-dependent behavior, showing DiffuMamba-H consistently improves at larger scales
Honest and transparent limitations: Appendix B clearly articulates important constraints (no block-training, fixed p assumption, batch size B=1) without over-claiming results
Appropriate architectural design: Bidirectional Mamba with additive fusion is well-motivated for diffusion's bidirectional conditioning requirements
weaknesses: Limited architectural novelty: Core contribution applies existing Mamba backbones to discrete DLMs—a straightforward engineering effort rather than methodological innovation. Hybrid variant trivially interleaves attention every N layers

Incomplete evaluation of best strategy: Models identified as most efficient (block-AR + Mamba, Figures 2c-d) were not trained with block-diffusion objectives, leaving efficiency potential unrealized and findings incomplete

Performance degradation at smaller scales: Pure DiffuMamba underperforms DiffuTran on 4 of 7 benchmarks at 240M (Table 1), suggesting unexplained scale dependencies that contradict claims of consistent advantages
Modest downstream improvements: ~4% average gain on reasoning tasks (Table 4) at 1.3B scale where all models struggle (<40% scores), providing weak evidence for quality preservation
Missing critical ablation studies: No exploration of interleaving frequency (N fixed at 5), state dimension sensitivity, or MLP expansion ratio impact, limiting understanding of design choices

Limited analysis of mechanistic understanding: Paper doesn't investigate whether improvements stem from selective SSM dynamics, structured recurrence, or other properties; lacks comparison to other linear-time mixers

Throughput evaluation limitations: Batch size B=1 is unrealistic for many deployments; fixed K=L/p doesn't account for adaptive stopping; no error bars reported; comparisons to AR baselines use different assumptions (block caching)

Incomplete reproducibility: No mention of code/model release plans; some implementation details missing (exact BiMamba fusion during inference, Mamba-2 version); no error bars on throughput despite averaging over 5 runs

Performance-efficiency tradeoff unclear: Relationship between quality and speed not thoroughly characterized, especially given 4% downstream gains vs. 8.2× throughput and downstream variability across scales
